tender.title: National Framework Agreement for the provision of Sexual Health Services
tender.description:
The demand for accessible, high-quality and innovative sexual health services continues to evolve in response to changing population needs, advances in clinical practice, increasing digital delivery models and the ongoing focus on reducing health inequalities.
The Framework will provide Relevant Authorities with a fully compliant route for the provision of sexual health services, supporting the commissioning of integrated, digital, clinical, diagnostic, prevention, outreach and specialist support services. The Framework is designed to enable Contracting Authorities to secure services that improve public health outcomes, promote early intervention and prevention, support vulnerable populations, and ensure equitable access to care. 
The overall aim of the Framework is to provide a compliant route to market facilitating the procurement of various Sexual Health Services. 
The Framework has been established under The Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023 and The Health Services (Provider Selection Regime) (Wales) Regulations 2025 (and as amended) (together the PSR) for use by all Relevant Authorities (and any future successors to these organisations).
"Relevant Authority" is defined in section 12ZB(7) of the National Health Service Act 2006 and in section 10A(9) of the National Health Service (Wales) Act 2006. It means a combined authority, an integrated care board, a local authority in England, NHS England, an NHS foundation trust or an NHS trust established under section 25 of the National Health Service Act 2006, a county council or county borough council in Wales, a local health board established under section 11 of the National Health Service (Wales) Act 2006, a National Health Service trust established under section 18 of the National Health Service (Wales) Act 2006, or a special health authority established under section 22 of the National Health Service (Wales) Act 2006. 
For the avoidance of doubt, any successor bodies of any of the above entities shall be entitled to place Orders and shall be deemed Relevant Authorities for the purposes of this Framework.
The Framework will be re-opened to new applicants every two years, approximately 90 days before the anniversary of the Framework Commencement Date.

tender.title: CeTPD Laboratory Information Management System
tender.description:
The Centre for Targeted Protein Degradation (CeTPD) is an academic research center focused on translational chemical biology, currently housing ~60 researchers and technicians across disciplines and experience levels (undergraduate, post graduate students, post-docs, (senior) staff scientists, Principal Investigators). The requirement is a software solution, for all research staff, that provides Laboratory Information Management System (LIMs) capability. This broadly includes scientist electronic lab notebook (across disciplines), reagent inventory and management, compound inventory and management and ideally some capability for processed data databasing and rudimentary visualisation.
We are seeking to procure a secure, cloud-based design and Laboratory Information Management System to support collaborative drug discovery workflows.
The solution is expected to deliver;
- An integrated platform for electronic lab notebooks, reagent inventory management, compound registration and management and ideally data visualisation.
- The system must accommodate the needs of scientists in both chemical and biological sciences and their respective workflows.
- The system must accommodate that Users may require access relevant to both chemical biological sciences workflows within the same user area.
- Seamless integration with existing computational workflows
- Seamless integration with third-party applications and/or databases
- A secure, stable and scalable cloud deployment which
Complies with the University and collaborator cybersecurity, information governance and GDPR requirements
Meets with strict performance, reliability and governance standards
Meets with the functional and non-functional requirements of the CeTPD (as outlined below)
- Improved operational efficiency, regulatory compliance, and scalability to support future growth and evolving scientific needs

- Port Infrastructure Works

criteria.description:
Bidders will be required to have a minimum "general" yearly turnover of 80,000 GBP for the last 3 years.
East Ayrshire Council reserve the right to review the bidders financial information including information from a credit reference agency (CreditSafe) at tender stage and for the duration of the contract, and seek clarifications if necessary.  If clarifications are not satisfactory the bidder may be excluded from the tender process.  It is the Tenderers responsibility to ensure that all information held by CreditSafe is current and accurate when submitting their tender.  The Council will not enter into discussions with Tenderers who fail to ensure that their CreditSafe scores are accurate by the due submission date.
It is a requirement of this contract that bidders hold, or can commit to obtain prior to the commencement of any subsequently awarded contract, the types and levels of insurance indicated below.
Employers' Liability Insurance = 10,000,000 GBP
Public Liability Insurance = 5,000,000 GBP
Product Liability Insurance = 5,000,000 GBP
Motor Vehicle Insurance

Bidders will be required to provide 2 examples of service carried out in the past three years that demonstrate that they have the relevant experience to deliver the service as described in part II.2.4 of this Contract Notice.  The Service should be of similar value, size and scope.
Bidders must provide contact details for each experience example.  The named Contacts  may be contacted to discuss the contract and the performance of the Service Provider.  Any Service Provider which fails to have have performed satisfactorily in the experience example may be excluded from the tender process.

Quality Management Requirements
The bidder must hold a UKAS (or equivalent) accredited independent third party certificate of compliance in accordance with BS EN ISO 9001 (or equivalent),
OR
The bidder must have a regularly reviewed documented policy regarding quality management.
Health and Safety Requirements
The bidder must hold a UKAS (or equivalent) accredited independent third party certificate of compliance in accordance with BS EN ISO 45001 (or equivalent) or have, within the last 12 months, successfully met the assessment requirements of a construction-related scheme in registered membership of the Safety Schemes in Procurement (SSIP) forum,
OR
The bidder must have a regularly reviewed and documented policy for Health and Safety (H&S) management.  Bidders that do not hold the relevant H&S Accreditation must download, complete and return EAC's Health and Safety Questionnaire.
Environmental Management Requirements
The bidder must hold a UKAS (or equivalent) accredited independent third party certificate of compliance with BE EN ISO 14001 (or equivalent) or a valid EMAS (or equivalent) certificate,
OR
The bidder must have a documented policy regarding environmental management.
Please refer to the attached document within PCS-T at Questions 1.72 and 1.74 of the SPD for further information.
